how_to_author: Read get_canonical_schema: the id column, this agent's bound fields (outputs only), and every other column with its type and tier.
Write the contract document in its final form from the API's documentation, following the template and the samples.
Call submit_contract with the document. On invalid or gate_failed, apply the fix each error carries and submit again. On failed, read the evidence, adjust the document, and submit again.
When the response says verified, call activate_contract with that version.

template.feed_type: product | review | store | content  (the agent's feed type)
template.credential: service | user  (service: the standing token registered in Studio; user: the signed-in person's token from the auth broker)
template.service_header: with service: the header that carries the standing token
template.service_value_format: with service: the header value with {token} where the token goes, exactly as the API wants it, e.g. "Bearer {token}" or "{token}"
template.user_header: with user: the header that carries the signed-in person's token
template.user_value_format: with user: the header value with {token} where that token goes

request.body: POST only: the JSON body, any nesting
_values: "{<id column>}"  GET only: the id list as one comma-separated value. REQUIRED, exactly once.

[ { "k": "{<id column>}", "c": "{<ingested column>}" } ]  POST only: one object per row, always a list of objects even for one id. REQUIRED, exactly once. An ingested column placeholder may sit only here.
"{_meta.openai/locale}"  chat context, sent whole; key dropped when the host has none.
"USD" / true / 3  literal, copied as written, never validated.

response._note: dictated: every API answers in this envelope

data.<key>: <flat value>  (one flat object per answered id)

fields._note: first entry REQUIRED: the feed type's id column (the echo); then only fields bound to this agent, at least one of them
fields.at: $.data[*].<key>  (where the value sits in each data item)
fields.type: string | int | float | boolean | image  (filled from the schema if omitted)
fields.default_value: used when an item lacks the key; empty = no value for that row

template.sample_request: the concrete query (GET) or body (POST) with real ids; sent as-is, once, to verify
template.test_user_token: with user only: a dummy token that belongs to no one, sent per user_header / user_value_format for the one verification call; never stored

response_rules: status success: the items in data apply. Ids listed in errors got no answer and their rows show no live value.
status failure: the whole call failed. Nothing is applied. errors says why.
The response must carry Cache-Control: no-store.
Every item carries the id it answers for. There is no one-value-for-all-rows form.
Items are flat: one level of keys, scalar values. Extra keys are ignored.
rules: The id placeholder is {<id column>} and appears exactly once in every request; every data item echoes the id. It is written the way the wire looks: on GET the query value itself, which becomes the batch's ids joined by commas; on POST inside the one object of a one-element list, which becomes one object per row. A bare placeholder or a plain list of ids on POST is refused.

An ingested column placeholder ({category}) may sit only inside that per-row object next to the id. POST only. A field bound to any realtime agent is never an input. The composition this agent belongs to must map the column. Its screen 2 (Schema Mapping) checks that before publish. After publish, a version with an unmapped input cannot be activated.
fields lists the id column first, then only fields bound to this agent: at least one of them, at most all of them. Fields bound to another agent, unbound fields and mandatory-tier fields are refused.

{_meta.*} is one value per call, inserted whole wherever it sits, also inside per-row objects. The key is dropped when the host sends none. Never sent at verification. Allowed keys: _meta.openai/locale, _meta.openai/userLocation.
Literal values are copied exactly, any JSON type, never validated.
One batch is one call. A batch larger than max_ids_per_call is split into consecutive calls of that size. Nothing else fans out.

credential names whose token every call carries; it must equal the agent's registered credential. For that kind the document says exactly how the token is sent: <kind>_header and <kind>_value_format with {token} exactly once. The platform adds nothing of its own. No token ever appears in the document: the standing token is read from the parameter store, the user's token comes from the auth broker per call.

Verification sends sample_request unchanged and reads the sent ids from it by matching the request template. It checks HTTP 2xx, Cache-Control: no-store, status success, every sent id appearing exactly once at the id field's path, and every field resolving to a value of its type or falling back to its default. A service contract verifies with the standing token; a user contract verifies with test_user_token, a dummy token that is used once and discarded.
Stored: the document as submitted minus test_user_token; type filled from the schema when omitted.
not_supported: Contracts without an id (one value for all rows, e.g. an account balance), nested values inside data items, composite keys, map-shaped responses, single-id endpoints, paginated responses. Such an API needs an adapter that presents this shape.
lifecycle: Every submit_contract call creates a new contract. A document that passes validation, the gates and the live check is stored as a new numbered version with status verified. A document that fails any of them is stored as failed with no version; the errors or the evidence come back in the response. Fix the document and submit again.
list_contracts lists the verified versions and names the active one.

activate_contract(version) re-runs the gates and the live check for that version, then makes it active; the previously active version becomes retired. Only a verified version can be activated. On a published composition, a version whose {column} inputs the composition does not map is refused: that needs a new realtime agent.
failed and retired are final. To go back to an older document, submit it again.
